title: An operator door that ends one attempt's WorkerAgent host on demand, so the host-loss fault can be injected mid-tool
gloss: kill a worker host on demand
description: 9if's first fault (the WorkerAgent DO's life lost mid-tool) is injected today by triggering a factory deploy (gh workflow run deploy-factory.yml). On 2026-10-07 that took ~10 min from trigger to swap (17:01-17:11 UTC), so it landed between tool calls of ex6's gzw and proved nothing; only a tool call longer than a deploy could be hit. Add an operator-only, authenticated factory route + CLI (e.g. ticfac cloud fault <run> --tick <t> host-loss) that ends exactly that attempt's WorkerAgent host life (abort the DO / drop its in-memory host) without touching the container, so the next heartbeat's host life must resume from storage and reattach the tracked bash by nonce. Exact identity only (run+tick+attempt), refuse the orchestrator. Update docs/pi-durable-cloud-run-runbook.md to use it.
acceptance_criteria: the door ends one named attempt's host mid-tool; the attempt's log then shows 'a new host life resumed the conversation from its storage' and the in-flight tool ran once; refuses any other run's attempt and the orchestrator; vitest + Go tests; runbook updated; make gate
